passages.title: How a Neural Network Learns
passages.content:
# A small neural network

A neural network transforms input numbers into predictions. Each layer multiplies its inputs by *weights*, adds a bias, and applies an activation function. The weights are learned from examples rather than written by hand.

## One training step

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Input] --> B[Prediction]
  B --> C[Calculate loss]
  C --> D[Update weights]
  D --> B
```

The loss measures the difference between a prediction and its target. A common loss for a numeric target is mean squared error:

$$L = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n}(y_i - \hat{y}_i)^2$$

An optimizer uses information from the loss to adjust the weights. It repeats this process over many training examples. A low training loss does **not** prove that the model will work well on new data; use a separate validation set.

```python
for batch in training_data:
    prediction = model(batch.inputs)
    loss = loss_function(prediction, batch.targets)
    update_weights(loss)
```

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Weight | A learned number that changes a layer's output |
| Loss | A measure of prediction error |

This practice guide is original learning material, not a framework-specific implementation.
